CHAPTER 1.1 · LEARNING AREA 1 · AUGUST · SEPTEMBER

Terms and transforming terms

A class is planning a trip: the coach costs €240, admission €6 per person. What does the class pay for 24, for 28, for 30 people? Instead of thinking it through again every time, you write down a term once: $240 + 6 \cdot x$. Then you only substitute. In this chapter you calculate with such terms, negative numbers included, and transform them until they are as simple as possible.

8 LESSONS3 UNITS2 LABS
WHAT YOU WILL LEARN IN THIS CHAPTER
  • write and read terms with variables
  • work out values of terms for positive and negative numbers, in formulas and tables of values
  • collect like terms and remove brackets
  • multiply out and factorise a common factor

$-12$

$5$

$30$: minus times minus gives plus.

$-6$

EXPLORATIONSTO GET STARTED · IN GROUPS
MATCHSTICK PATTERNS

Lay out squares of matchsticks in a row: one square needs 4 matches, two squares need 7, three need 10.

  • How many matches do you need for 10 squares, how many for $n$ squares?
  • Compare your terms. Are they different or only written differently?
→ Units 1 and 2
A NUMBER TRICK

Think of a number. Add 3, double the result, subtract 6 and halve.

  • Try it with several numbers, negative ones too. What do you notice?
  • Can you explain why it always works?
→ Unit 3
ONE BED, TWO WAYS

A flower bed is 4 m wide. It consists of a 6 m long part with tomatoes and a 3 m long part with herbs.

  • Work out the area of the whole bed in two different ways.
  • What happens if the tomato part is $x$ metres long?
→ Unit 3
UNIT 14 LESSONS

1Terms and values of terms

On the trip, the costs depend on the number of people. For this number you write a variable, for example $x$. The term $240 + 6 \cdot x$ then describes the costs in euros for every group size. For 24 people you substitute $x = 24$: $240 + 6 \cdot 24 = 384$.

KEY POINT · TERMS AND VALUES OF TERMS

A term is a meaningful expression made of numbers, variables, operation signs and brackets, for example $3x + 5$, $2 \cdot (a + b)$ or $x^2 - 1$.

If you substitute a number for the variable and work it out, you get the value of the term.

You substitute negative numbers in brackets: for $x = -2$, $3x + 5 = 3 \cdot (-2) + 5 = -1$.

The rule is: brackets first, then powers, then multiplication and division before addition and subtraction.

Multiplication dot: it may be left out between a number and a variable: $3x$ means $3 \cdot x$.

Spreadsheet: if $x$ is in cell A2, the formula =3*A2+5 in B2 works out the value of the term. Filling down gives many values at once.

INTERACTIVE · THE CALCULATION TREE OF A TERM

Choose a value for $x$. The numbers travel from the bottom to the top: the operation done last gives the term its name.

EXAMPLE 1 · SUBSTITUTING A NEGATIVE NUMBER

Work out the value of the term $2x^2 - 3x$ for $x = -3$.

$2 \cdot (-3)^2 - 3 \cdot (-3) = 2 \cdot 9 + 9 = 18 + 9$

The value of the term is $27$.

Careful: $(-3)^2 = 9$, because minus times minus gives plus. And $-3 \cdot (-3) = +9$.

EXAMPLE 2 · THE TRIP

The coach costs €240, admission €6 per person. What does the trip cost for 24 people in total and per person?

Costs: $240 + 6 \cdot 24 = 240 + 144 = 384$, so €384. Per person: $384 : 24 = 16$.

€384 in total, €16 per person.

EXERCISES

Work out the value of the term $4x - 7$ for a) $x = 3$   b) $x = 0$   c) $x = -2$   d) $x = 0.5$.

a) $5$   b) $-7$   c) $4 \cdot (-2) - 7 = -15$   d) $2 - 7 = -5$

Write a term. a) three times a number, decreased by 4   b) the sum of a number and its double   c) the perimeter of a rectangle with the sides $a$ and $b$   d) the price of $x$ exercise books at €1.20 and a pad at €2.50

a) $3x - 4$   b) $x + 2x$   c) $2a + 2b$ or $2 \cdot (a + b)$   d) $1.2x + 2.5$ (in euros)

Make a table of values for the term $x^2 - 2x$ for $x = -2,\ -1,\ 0,\ 1,\ 2,\ 3$. For which numbers is the value of the term 0?

Values: $8,\ 3,\ 0,\ -1,\ 0,\ 3$. The value of the term is 0 for $x = 0$ and $x = 2$.

The area of a trapezium is $A = (a + c) \cdot h : 2$. Work out $A$ for a) $a = 7\,\text{cm}$, $c = 3\,\text{cm}$, $h = 4\,\text{cm}$   b) $a = 5.5\,\text{cm}$, $c = 2.5\,\text{cm}$, $h = 3\,\text{cm}$.

a) $(7 + 3) \cdot 4 : 2 = 20$, so $20\,\text{cm}^2$   b) $(5.5 + 2.5) \cdot 3 : 2 = 12$, so $12\,\text{cm}^2$

For $n$ squares in a row you need $3n + 1$ matches. a) How many matches is that for 25 squares?   b) How many squares can you lay out with 100 matches?   c) Lena writes $4 + 3 \cdot (n - 1)$. Is she right too? Give a reason.

a) $3 \cdot 25 + 1 = 76$ matches.   b) $3 \cdot 33 + 1 = 100$: exactly 33 squares.   c) Yes: the first square needs 4 matches, every further one 3. And $4 + 3n - 3 = 3n + 1$.

TEST YOURSELF!

Work out the value of $5 - 2x$ for $x = -4$.

$5 - 2 \cdot (-4) = 5 + 8 = 13$

Work out the value of $x^2 + x$ for $x = -3$.

$(-3)^2 + (-3) = 9 - 3 = 6$

A taxi costs a basic fare of €4 and €2.50 per kilometre. What does a 12 km ride cost?

$4 + 2.5 \cdot 12 = 34$, so €34.

UNIT 22 LESSONS

2Collecting terms and removing brackets

A rectangle has the sides $x$ and $x + 3$. Its perimeter is $x + (x + 3) + x + (x + 3)$. It can be written more briefly: four times $x$ and twice 3, so $4x + 6$. Both terms give the same value for every $x$. Such terms are called equivalent.

KEY POINT · TRANSFORMING TERMS

Like terms have the same variable with the same exponent. Only they may be collected: $3x + 5x = 8x$, but $3x + 5$ stays as it is.

Plus before a bracket: if there is a plus sign in front of the bracket, you may leave out the bracket: $a + (b - c) = a + b - c$.

Minus before a bracket: if there is a minus sign in front of the bracket, all the signs inside change when you leave it out: $a - (b - c) = a - b + c$.

Equivalent terms have the same value for every number substituted.

Sorting helps: first all the terms with $x$, then the numbers. The sign always belongs to the term after it.

Don’t mix up: $x + x = 2x$, but $x \cdot x = x^2$.

INTERACTIVE · EQUIVALENT OR NOT?

Choose a pair of terms and compare their values. A single counterexample is enough to show that two terms are not equivalent.

EXAMPLE 3 · COLLECTING TERMS

Simplify $7x + 4 - 2x - 9 + x$.

Sort: $7x - 2x + x + 4 - 9$. The terms with $x$: $7 - 2 + 1 = 6$. The numbers: $4 - 9 = -5$.

$7x + 4 - 2x - 9 + x = 6x - 5$

EXAMPLE 4 · A MINUS BEFORE A BRACKET

Simplify $12a - (5a - 3) + (2 - a)$.

The minus before the first bracket turns both signs round, the bracket with a plus simply disappears: $12a - 5a + 3 + 2 - a$.

$12a - (5a - 3) + (2 - a) = 6a + 5$

Check with $a = 1$: $12 - 2 + 1 = 11$ and $6 + 5 = 11$.

EXERCISES

Collect like terms. a) $4x + 9x$   b) $6y - 8y + y$   c) $3a + 5 - a + 2$   d) $2.5x - 0.5 + 1.5x$

a) $13x$   b) $-y$   c) $2a + 7$   d) $4x - 0.5$

Remove the bracket and collect like terms. a) $8 + (x - 3)$   b) $8 - (x - 3)$   c) $5x - (2x + 7)$   d) $-(4 - y) + 6$

a) $x + 5$   b) $11 - x$   c) $3x - 7$   d) $y + 2$

Which terms are equivalent? A: $2x + 3x$   B: $5x$   C: $5 + x$   D: $x + x + x + x + x$   E: $x^5$. Show with a counterexample that the others do not belong.

A, B and D are equivalent. Counterexample $x = 2$: A, B and D give 10, C gives 7, E gives 32.

Tim calculates: $10x - (4x - 6) = 10x - 4x - 6 = 6x - 6$. Find the mistake, correct it and check with $x = 1$.

The minus before the bracket turns the second sign round too: $10x - 4x + 6 = 6x + 6$. Check: $10 - (4 - 6) = 12$ and $6 + 6 = 12$, whereas Tim’s term gives 0.

A rectangle has the sides $x$ and $x + 4$ (in cm). a) Give the perimeter as a term that is as simple as possible.   b) Work out the perimeter for $x = 3.5$.   c) For which $x$ is the perimeter 40 cm? Try it out.

a) $2x + 2 \cdot (x + 4) = 4x + 8$   b) $4 \cdot 3.5 + 8 = 22$, so 22 cm   c) $4 \cdot 8 + 8 = 40$: $x = 8$. How to solve this without trying out, you will learn in chapter 1.2.

TEST YOURSELF!

Collect like terms: $9x - 4x + 2x = \square\, x$. Which number goes in the box?

$9 - 4 + 2 = 7$, so $7x$.

Remove the bracket: $15 - (6 - x) = \square + x$. Which number goes in the box?

$15 - 6 + x = 9 + x$

Which term is equivalent to $3 - (x - 2)$?

$3 - x + 2 = 5 - x$

UNIT 32 LESSONS

3Multiplying out and factorising

The bed is 4 m wide and $6\,\text{m} + 3\,\text{m}$ long. Its area is $4 \cdot (6 + 3) = 36$. You can also work out both parts separately: $4 \cdot 6 + 4 \cdot 3 = 24 + 12 = 36$. With $x$ instead of 6 this means: $4 \cdot (x + 3) = 4x + 12$.

KEY POINT · THE DISTRIBUTIVE LAW

Multiplying out: every term in the bracket is multiplied by the factor:

$a \cdot (b + c) = a \cdot b + a \cdot c \qquad a \cdot (b - c) = a \cdot b - a \cdot c$

Factorising: if all the terms have a common factor, you take it out in front of the bracket: $6x + 15 = 3 \cdot (2x + 5)$.

With a negative factor the signs change: $-2 \cdot (x - 4) = -2x + 8$.

Don’t forget a term: $3 \cdot (x + 1) = 3x + 3$, not $3x + 1$.

Checking a factorisation: multiply out again. You must get back the term you started with.

INTERACTIVE · A PRODUCT AS AN AREA

Change $a$, $b$ and $c$. Switch to “with x” and read the equation once from left to right (multiplying out) and once from right to left (factorising).

EXAMPLE 5 · MULTIPLYING OUT AND COLLECTING

Simplify $4 \cdot (2x - 3) - 3 \cdot (x - 5)$.

The factor $-3$ applies to both terms of the second bracket: $8x - 12 - 3x + 15$.

$4 \cdot (2x - 3) - 3 \cdot (x - 5) = 5x + 3$

EXAMPLE 6 · FACTORISING

Take out the highest common factor: $14x - 21$.

14 and 21 are both divisible by 7: $14x = 7 \cdot 2x$ and $21 = 7 \cdot 3$.

$14x - 21 = 7 \cdot (2x - 3)$

Check: $7 \cdot 2x - 7 \cdot 3 = 14x - 21$.

EXERCISES

Multiply out. a) $5 \cdot (x + 4)$   b) $3 \cdot (2a - 7)$   c) $-4 \cdot (y - 2)$   d) $0.5 \cdot (8x + 6)$

a) $5x + 20$   b) $6a - 21$   c) $-4y + 8$   d) $4x + 3$

Take out the highest common factor. a) $4x + 12$   b) $15a - 10$   c) $9y + 27$   d) $8x - 8$

a) $4 \cdot (x + 3)$   b) $5 \cdot (3a - 2)$   c) $9 \cdot (y + 3)$   d) $8 \cdot (x - 1)$

Simplify. a) $2 \cdot (x + 5) + 3 \cdot (x - 1)$   b) $6 \cdot (a - 2) - 4 \cdot (a - 3)$   c) $7 - 2 \cdot (3 - y)$

a) $2x + 10 + 3x - 3 = 5x + 7$   b) $6a - 12 - 4a + 12 = 2a$   c) $7 - 6 + 2y = 1 + 2y$

A flower bed is 3 m wide and $x$ m long. Next to it there is a piece of lawn, also 3 m wide and 5 m long. Write the total area as a product and as a sum. Work it out for $x = 7$.

$3 \cdot (x + 5) = 3x + 15$ (in $\text{m}^2$). For $x = 7$: $3 \cdot 12 = 36$, so $36\,\text{m}^2$.

Explain the number trick from the explorations with a term: think of a number $x$, add 3, double, subtract 6, halve.

$2 \cdot (x + 3) = 2x + 6$. Minus 6 gives $2x$, halved gives $x$. You always get back the number you thought of, negative numbers included.

TEST YOURSELF!

Multiply out: $6 \cdot (x - 3) = 6x - \square$. Which number goes in the box?

$6 \cdot 3 = 18$

Factorise: $21x + 35 = 7 \cdot (3x + \square)$. Which number goes in the box?

$35 : 7 = 5$

Work out the value of $-3 \cdot (2 - x)$ for $x = 4$.

$-3 \cdot (2 - 4) = -3 \cdot (-2) = 6$

REVIEW · DEEPEN · CONNECT

Work out the value of $3 \cdot (x - 2) - x$ for $x = -1$. Then simplify the term and substitute again.

$3 \cdot (-3) + 1 = -8$. Simplified: $2x - 6$, and $2 \cdot (-1) - 6 = -8$.

Connect with Year 7: a bike costs $x$ euros. It becomes 20 % more expensive, later 20 % cheaper. Write a term for the final price and simplify it. Is the bike as expensive again as at the start?

$0.8 \cdot 1.2 \cdot x = 0.96x$. In the end the bike is 4 % cheaper than at the start.

In a spreadsheet, cells A2 to A8 hold the numbers −3 to 3. Which formula goes in B2 for the term $2 \cdot (x - 1) + 4$? Which value is in B8? Which simpler term gives the same column?

=2*(A2-1)+4. In B8, for $x = 3$, there is the value $2 \cdot 2 + 4 = 8$. Simpler: $2x + 2$.

Triangles of matchsticks in a row, alternately pointing up and down: one triangle needs 3 matches, two need 5, three need 7. Write a term for $n$ triangles and work out the number of matches for 50 triangles.

$3 + 2 \cdot (n - 1) = 2n + 1$. For 50 triangles: $101$ matches.

EXCURSIONHISTORY

Plus and minus from Leipzig

The signs + and − appear for the first time in a printed book that was published in Leipzig in 1489: Behende und hübsche Rechenung auff allen Kauffmanschafft (“Quick and neat calculation for all trades”) by Johannes Widmann. Widmann taught at the University of Leipzig, and in 1486 he gave the first lectures on algebra at a German university there. In his arithmetic book, + and − do not yet mean “add” and “subtract”, but a surplus and a shortfall, for example in the weight of goods.

About a hundred years later, the Frenchman François Viète used letters for numbers systematically. In his work In artem analyticem isagoge (1591) he wrote vowels for unknown and consonants for known quantities. That today we take $x$, $y$ and $z$ for unknowns and $a$, $b$, $c$ for known numbers goes back to René Descartes and his Géométrie of 1637.

Sources: J. Widmann, Behende und hübsche Rechenung auff allen Kauffmanschafft, Leipzig 1489 (Neue Deutsche Biographie, article “Widmann, Johannes”). F. Viète, In artem analyticem isagoge, Tours 1591. R. Descartes, La Géométrie, Leiden 1637.

LOOKING BACKTHE ESSENTIALS AT A GLANCE

VALUE OF A TERM

substitute the number, negative numbers in brackets, brackets before powers before multiplication before addition

$x = -2$: $3x + 5 = -1$

COLLECTING TERMS

only like terms

$7x + 4 - 2x - 9 = 5x - 5$

REMOVING BRACKETS

with a plus in front the bracket disappears, with a minus in front all the signs turn round

$a - (b - c) = a - b + c$

MULTIPLYING OUT · FACTORISING

every term times the factor, and backwards

$3 \cdot (2x + 5) = 6x + 15$

TESTTWO ROUNDS · INSTANT FEEDBACK
ROUND 1 · IN YOUR HEAD

Work out the value of $3x - 5$ for $x = -2$.

$-6 - 5 = -11$

Collect like terms: $4a + 7 - a - 2 = 3a + \square$. Which number goes in the box?

$7 - 2 = 5$

Which term is equivalent to $2 \cdot (x + 5)$?

$2x + 10$: both terms are multiplied by 2.

ROUND 2 · THINK IT THROUGH

Work out the value of $20 - (8 - x)$ for $x = 5$.

$20 - 3 = 17$, or simplified $12 + x = 17$.

Factorise: $16x - 24 = 8 \cdot (2x - \square)$. Which number goes in the box?

$24 : 8 = 3$

Simplify: $5 \cdot (x - 2) - 3 \cdot (x - 4) = 2x + \square$. Which number goes in the box?

$5x - 10 - 3x + 12 = 2x + 2$
